system_title: Government Civic & Public Welfare Knowledge Base

documents.topic: Potholes, Damaged Roads and Asphalt Collapse Redressal
documents.act_or_scheme: Karnataka Municipal Corporations (KMC) Act & Sakala Guarantee
documents.content: Road maintenance, pothole filling, and footpath repairs in municipal zones fall under the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) Road Infrastructure division or local Municipal Corporation. Under the Sakala Services Act, critical potholes causing imminent hazard must be addressed within 48 hours. Citizens can report road damage through this portal or via BBMP FixPothole app. For arterial and major roads, the Executive Engineer (Road Infrastructure) is the designated nodal officer. If accidents occur due to unbarricaded road cuts or neglected potholes, the municipal engineer on duty is held accountable under civic safety guidelines.
documents.escalation: Level 1: Ward Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) -> Level 2: Executive Engineer (Roads) -> Level 3: Joint Commissioner (Zone) -> Level 4: Karnataka Lokayukta
documents.action_suggested: Submit complaint under 'Mobility - Roads & Infrastructure' with photo evidence for priority dispatch.

documents.topic: Solid Waste Management, Roadside Dumping & Segregation Guidelines
documents.act_or_scheme: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 & Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)
documents.content: Municipal corporations mandate door-to-door waste collection with strict two-bin one-bag source segregation: Green bin for wet/biodegradable organic waste, White/Blue bag for dry recyclable waste, and Red sanitary pouch for domestic hazardous waste. Roadside black spots and unattended garbage heaps are violations punishable by fines ranging from Rs 500 for first-time individual offenders up to Rs 25,000 for commercial bulk generators. Complaints regarding missed door-to-door collection or roadside dumps have a mandatory resolution SLA of 24 hours. The local Junior Health Inspector (JHI) is responsible for clearing the spot and disinfecting with bleaching powder.
documents.escalation: Level 1: Junior Health Inspector (JHI) -> Level 2: Senior Health Inspector (SHI) -> Level 3: Assistant Executive Engineer (SWM) -> Level 4: Chief Engineer (SWM)
documents.action_suggested: Submit complaint under 'Public Cleanliness / Sanitation' with photo evidence to clear black spot.

documents.topic: Streetlight Non-Functional, Dark Spots & Timer Faults
documents.act_or_scheme: Street Lighting National Programme (SLNP) & Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL)
documents.content: Streetlighting on public thoroughfares, parks, and residential layouts is managed through public-private partnerships under the Street Lighting National Programme (SLNP) with energy-efficient LED luminaires and Centralized Control and Monitoring Systems (CCMS). Individual non-functional lamps have an official restoration SLA of 36 hours. Circuit-level phase failures affecting an entire street or junction have an emergency SLA of 12 hours. Citizens must note the pole number or nearby landmark when lodging complaints to expedite maintenance van dispatch.
documents.escalation: Level 1: Ward Electrical Supervisor -> Level 2: Assistant Executive Engineer (Electrical) -> Level 3: Executive Engineer (Electrical Works)
documents.action_suggested: Submit complaint under 'Street Lighting & Electrical' specifying nearest pole number or landmark.

documents.topic: Drinking Water Disruption, Pipeline Leakages & Contamination
documents.authority: BWSSB (Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board) / Urban Water Board
documents.act_or_scheme: Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban), AMRUT 2.0 & BWSSB Act 1964
documents.content: BWSSB and municipal water utilities are legally obligated to supply potable drinking water complying with IS 10500 standards. Water supply disruptions due to valve faults, pipeline bursts, or schedule maintenance must be notified in advance. Contaminated (murky or foul-smelling) water supply triggers an immediate bio-chemical inspection within 12 hours due to public health risks of waterborne diseases like cholera and typhoid. Pipeline bursts and roadway washouts have an emergency response SLA of 6 hours for isolation and 24 hours for full restoration. Under AMRUT 2.0 and Jal Jeevan Mission, 100% universal metering and functional household tap connections (FHTC) are guaranteed.
documents.escalation: Level 1: Service Station Water Inspector -> Level 2: Assistant Executive Engineer (Water Distribution) -> Level 3: Executive Engineer -> Level 4: Chief Engineer (Maintenance)
documents.action_suggested: Submit complaint under 'Water Supply & Distribution'. For contaminated water, mark priority as High/Urgent.

documents.topic: Power Outages, Low Hanging Cables, Transformer Sparks & Hazards
documents.authority: BESCOM (Bangalore Electricity Supply Company) / State DISCOM
documents.act_or_scheme: Electricity Act 2003 & Central Electricity Authority (Safety Requirements) Regulations
documents.content: Electricity distribution companies (DISCOMs) are bound by the Electricity Act 2003 and State Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC) service quality standards. Unscheduled power outages in urban areas must be resolved within 4 hours during normal conditions. Hazardous situations—such as snapped high-tension (11kV/66kV) wires, sparking distribution transformers, leaning electrical poles, or exposed junction boxes—are classified as Code-Red Emergencies requiring ground crew arrival within 30 minutes and complete rectification within 12 hours. Severe voltage fluctuations that damage household appliances can be registered for compensation inspection through the DISCOM Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF).
documents.escalation: Level 1: BESCOM 24x7 Helpline 1912 / Local Section Officer (SO) -> Level 2: Assistant Executive Engineer (O&M) -> Level 3: Superintending Engineer -> Level 4: Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF)
documents.action_suggested: Submit complaint under 'Electricity & Power Supply'. For hanging live wires or sparking, flag as Urgent Emergency.

documents.topic: Traffic Signal Malfunctions, Missing Signs, Speed Breakers & Road Hazards
documents.authority: Traffic Police / Transport Department / Municipal Traffic Engineering
documents.act_or_scheme: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019 & Indian Roads Congress (IRC:99) Guidelines
documents.content: Traffic engineering and safety enforcement operate jointly between the Traffic Police and the Municipal Traffic Engineering Cell (TEC). Malfunctioning traffic lights or signal controllers at busy junctions are addressed within 12 hours. Unauthorized or unscientific asphalt humps that violate IRC specifications (standard height: 10 cm, width: 3.5 m with parabolic profile and reflective thermoplastic markings) can be ordered for reconstruction or demolition. Citizens can also report traffic violations, footpath riding, and illegal commercial parking through the BTP Public Eye portal. Road safety audits are mandatory for any stretch with frequent fatal accidents.
documents.escalation: Level 1: Traffic Police Sub-Inspector (Jurisdictional) -> Level 2: Assistant Commissioner of Police (Traffic ACP) -> Level 3: DCP (Traffic)
documents.action_suggested: Submit complaint under 'Traffic & Road Safety' with exact intersection name and geo-coordinates.

documents.topic: Open Manholes, Sewage Overflow, Blocked UGD & Drainage Hazards
documents.authority: BWSSB Sewerage Division / Municipal Drainage Cell
documents.act_or_scheme: Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act 2013 & KMC Storm Water Act
documents.content: Underground drainage (UGD) network blockages causing sewage backflow onto public roads or into residential compounds pose severe sanitary hazards. Open or damaged manhole covers represent an extreme life-safety peril, especially during monsoon rains; municipal protocols dictate barricading within 2 hours and cover replacement within 12 to 24 hours. Under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act 2013, all sewer cleaning must strictly be mechanized using jetting and super-sucker machines. Stormwater drains (raja kaluves) must remain unencroached to prevent urban flooding.
documents.escalation: Level 1: Assistant Engineer (Sewerage Maintenance) -> Level 2: Assistant Executive Engineer (UGD) -> Level 3: Chief Engineer (Waste Water Management)
documents.action_suggested: Submit complaint under 'Drainage & Sewerage'. For missing manhole covers, mark priority as Urgent Emergency.

documents.topic: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (Rooftop Solar Subsidy)
documents.authority: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) / State DISCOMs
documents.act_or_scheme: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (2024)
documents.content: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is a flagship central scheme providing up to 300 units of free electricity per month to 1 crore households by providing heavy capital subsidies for residential rooftop solar installations. Central Government Subsidy Structure: 1 kW system receives Rs 30,000; 2 kW system receives Rs 60,000; systems of 3 kW or higher receive a maximum subsidy of Rs 78,000. Additionally, nationalized banks offer collateral-free loans at concessional interest rates (~7% p.a.). Citizens apply online via pmsuryaghar.gov.in, select an empaneled vendor, undergo DISCOM technical feasibility inspection, install the bi-directional net-meter, and receive direct subsidy credit (DBT) into their bank account within 30 days of commissioning.
documents.escalation: DISCOM Nodal Officer (Renewable Energy) -> State Nodal Agency (e.g. KREDL) -> MNRE Grievance Cell
documents.action_suggested: Explore scheme eligibility or register for rooftop solar feasibility with your state DISCOM.

documents.topic: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY - Urban 2.0 & Gramin)
documents.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
documents.content: PMAY provides all-weather pucca houses with basic civic amenities (water, electricity, toilet) to eligible urban and rural families belonging to EWS (Economically Weaker Sections, annual income up to Rs 3 Lakh), LIG (Low Income Groups, up to Rs 6 Lakh), and MIG categories. The scheme operates through 4 verticals: In-situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR), Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) offering interest subvention up to Rs 2.67 Lakh on housing loans, Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), and Beneficiary-led individual house Construction (BLC) providing direct financial assistance of Rs 1.5 Lakh to 2.5 Lakh. Applications are processed through urban local bodies (ULBs) and Common Service Centers (CSCs).
documents.escalation: Municipal Project Officer (Housing) -> District Collector / Deputy Commissioner -> State Housing Board
documents.action_suggested: Verify Aadhaar-linked eligibility at pmaymis.gov.in or consult local Municipal Housing Desk.

documents.topic: Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) & AMRUT 2.0 (Har Ghar Jal)
documents.authority: Ministry of Jal Shakti / State Rural & Urban Water Supply
documents.act_or_scheme: Jal Jeevan Mission & Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT 2.0)
documents.content: Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) is committed to providing Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) to every rural household, delivering 55 litres of water per capita per day (lpcd) of prescribed quality on a regular and long-term basis. AMRUT 2.0 covers all statutory towns to achieve universal coverage of water supply through water body rejuvenation, wastewater recycling, and digital water management. Gram Panchayats and Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSC) manage local operation and maintenance. Water quality testing kits are distributed to local women self-help groups (SHGs) for field testing of 12 chemical and bacteriological parameters.
documents.escalation: Gram Panchayat Secretary -> Executive Engineer (Rural Water Supply & Sanitation) -> Mission Director (JJM)
documents.action_suggested: Report missing tap water infrastructure or poor water quality under JJM monitoring cell.

documents.topic: Karnataka Sakala Services Act 2011 & Citizen Charters
documents.act_or_scheme: Karnataka Guarantee of Services to Citizens Act, 2011 (Sakala)
documents.content: The Sakala Act legally guarantees time-bound delivery of over 1,025 public services across 31 government departments in Karnataka. When a citizen submits a Sakala application or grievance, a unique 15-digit Guarantee of Services to Citizen (GSC) number is generated with an explicit statutory deadline. If the competent authority fails to deliver the service or resolve the grievance within the stipulated period, the citizen is entitled to compensatory cost of Rs 20 per day of delay (up to a maximum of Rs 500), deducted directly from the defaulting government officer's salary. Citizens can file a First Appeal to the designated Appellate Authority within 30 days of expiry of the due date.
documents.escalation: Competent Officer -> First Appellate Authority (FAA) -> Second Appellate Authority (SAA) -> Sakala Mission Director
documents.action_suggested: Track your statutory grievance timeline using your Complaint ID / GSC number.

documents.topic: CPGRAMS Central Grievance Portal & Escalation to Lokayukta
documents.authority: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)
documents.act_or_scheme: CPGRAMS Portal & Prevention of Corruption / Lokayukta Act
documents.content: CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in) is the single centralized grievance portal connecting over 90 Central Ministries, Departments, and State Governments. Grievances filed on CPGRAMS must be redressed within a maximum timeline of 30 days. If the resolution provided by the subordinate department is unsatisfactory or fictitious, the citizen has the statutory right to file an Appeal within 30 days, which is reviewed by an independent Senior Appellate Authority. For chronic civic neglect, harassment, corruption, or refusal to perform lawful duty, citizens can approach the State Lokayukta or Upalokayukta with an affidavit under the Lokayukta Act.
documents.escalation: Subordinate Officer -> Head of Department -> CPGRAMS Appellate Authority -> State Lokayukta
documents.action_suggested: If local municipal redressal has failed for over 30 days, file an escalation on CPGRAMS or Lokayukta.
